geometryProvenance.units: R, Z, x, y, z in m; B = |B| in T (absolute VMEC bmnc, not normalised by B_ref); rho, s and iota dimensionless; theta, phi and alpha in rad

verification.details: No external reference for these grids exists in this repo. They are evaluated with the VMEC reader and straight-field-line tracer that geometry.json validates against stella's saved rho 0.7 output (stella's radial interpolation; |B| and iota at rho 0 and rho 1 use its half-grid extrapolation). On the magnetic axis (rho 0) R and Z do not depend on theta, but |B| does: that extrapolation leaves the m > 0 |B| modes non-zero at s = 0, so within one phi plane the axis |B| varies with theta by up to 0.029 T (1.1 % of its mean 2.69 T); its theta mean on each plane is the m = 0 part. The diverter positions are schematic (the owner's four), not W7-X data.

grid.angles: theta_i = 2*pi*i/nTheta, i = 0..nTheta-1 (VMEC poloidal angle; theta = 0 outboard midplane, theta = pi/2 top, Z > 0); phi_j = 2*pi*j/nPhi, j = 0..nPhi-1 (geometric toroidal angle; x = R cos phi, y = R sin phi, z = Z); both periodic, no duplicated seam; flat index c = j*nTheta + i

model.discretization: LCFS grid of `grid` (nTheta θ × nPhi φ; every index periodic, i mod nTheta and j mod nPhi; cell c = j·nTheta + i), θ_i = 2πi/nTheta, φ_j = 2πj/nPhi, dθ = 2π/nTheta, dφ = 2π/nPhi. Inputs exactly as written in this artifact: B_s = surfaces[last].B (LCFS |B|, T), φ_k = diverters.items[k].phi, θ_d = diverters.thetaCentre, every parameter = model.parameters[name].value. wrap(x) = x − 2π·floor(x/(2π) + 0.5); g(x, σ) = exp(−x²/(2σ²)). t_n = n·Δt with n counted from the initial condition; the coils c_k of step n are those of the coil-schedule entry with the largest fromStep ≤ n. The edge is quasi-steady (its time scales, microseconds, are far below Δt): at t_n and for coils c: (1) a_k = c_k·cos(2πf·t_n); (2) h_k[c] = g(wrap(φ_j − φ_k), σ_cφ)·g(wrap(θ_i − θ_d), σ_cθ); (3) B[c] = B_s[c]·(1 + ε·Σ_k a_k·h_k[c]); (4) θ_s,k = θ_d + A_s·a_k; (6) s_k[j] = G_k[j]/Σ_m G_m[j], G_k[j] = g(wrap(φ_j − φ_k), π/N_div), u_k = mean_c s_k, f_k = 1 − η·c_k, P_k = P_heat·(1 − f_rad)·u_k·f_k·(Σ_m u_m)/(Σ_m u_m·f_m) (MW, sums in order m = 0…3); (7) j_k = round(φ_k/dφ) mod nPhi, x = θ_s,k/dθ, i₀ = floor(x), w = x − i₀, B_k = (1 − w)·B[j_k, i₀] + w·B[j_k, i₀+1], b_k = B_k/B_0; (8) q_t,k = P_k·b_k/(A_wet·w_k) (MW/m²); (8b) w_k = (T_u,k/T_λ)^e_λ (1 with no plasma); (9) Q_k[i] = q_t,k·g(wrap(θ_i − θ_s,k), σ_θ·w_k/b_k); (10) q_∥ = q_t,k·MW/sin α (W/m²; no power: q_t = T_u = T_t = 0, w = 1), X = ν·q_∥·L_c/κ_0, T_u = X^(1/ν) from w_k = 1, then N_2pt times: c = 2·q_∥/(γ·n_u·keV·T_u), T_t = m_i·amu·c²/(2·keV), T_u = (T_t^ν + X)^(1/ν) (keV), then w_k (8b), q_t,k (8), q_∥ and X with the new w_k (8, 8b, 10 solved together). One step n → n+1: (11) every strip cell k, i holds N_z tile cells S[z] (°C, z = 0 at the surface), dz = d/N_z, k(T) = k_ref/(1 + (T − T_ref)/T_k), c(T) = c_∞ − (c_∞ − c_ref)·exp(−(T − T_ref)/T_c), q = Q_k[i]·MW (W/m²) with Q_k at t_n and the coils of step n; G_z = 2·k_z·k_(z+1)/(dz·(k_z + k_(z+1))), F_z = G_z·(S[z] − S[z+1]), sink = (S[N_z−1] − T_cool)/(dz/(2k_(N_z−1)) + R_sink); net[0] = q, net[z] −= F_z, net[z+1] += F_z, net[N_z−1] −= sink (in that order); S[z] ← S[z] + Δt·net[z]/(ρ·c(S[z])·dz), with k and c of the old S; the surface temperature Tt_k[i] = S[0] + q·dz/(2·k(S[0])) from the new S[0]; (12) the new state's LCFS temperature at t_(n+1) with the same coils, T[c] = T_u[j] = Σ_k s_k[j]·T_u,k (the LCFS at the upstream temperature). The initial state: every tile cell and surface T_cool, T from (12) at t_0 with every coil off. Diagnostics of the state after n steps (golden checkpoints): t = n·Δt; probesT = T at each model.probes [i, j]; meanT = arithmetic mean of T over all cells; peakTileC[k] = max_i Tt_k[i]; peakHeatFlux[k] = max_i Q_k[i] at t_n with the coils of step n. Stability: the only explicit update is the tile conduction, monotone when Δt·max(2k_ref/dz, k_ref/dz + 1/(dz/(2k_ref) + R_sink))/(ρ·c_ref·dz) ≤ 1 (inner and back cell; k and c at T_ref bound every cell above T_ref ≤ T_cool); here 0.5189.

equations.meaning: Governing equation (used to predict how the heat moves): energy conservation. The heating power that is not radiated leaves through the divertors, each taking the share of its toroidal sector; a coil that is on moves the island and lowers its divertor's weight by 1 − η, and the shares are renormalised so the total never changes (one coil alone sheds ~24 %, every coil on moves nothing); the two-point model below turns each share into the target load and the edge temperatures.
equations.text: P_k = P_heat·(1 − f_rad)·u_k·f_k·Σ_m u_m / Σ_m u_m·f_m,  u_k = mean(s_k),  f_k = 1 − η·c_k,  s_k(φ) = G_k / Σ_m G_m,  G_k = g(φ − φ_k, π/N_div)

equations.meaning: Peak heat flux on target k (MW/m²): its power on the wetted area, compressed with |B| at the strike line (a flux tube's cross-section shrinks as 1/B); spread along the tile strip around the strike line, narrowed as 1/B, so the strip deposits exactly P_k. The footprint width follows the edge (version 8): λ_q = (χ_⊥τ_∥)^½ with the conduction-limited drain time τ_∥ ∝ L_c²n/(κ_0T_u^(5/2)), so a hotter edge gives a narrower footprint and a higher peak (a modelling choice: measured widths depend mainly on the poloidal field); solved together with the two-point model (they depend on each other).
equations.text: q_t,k = P_k·b_k/(A_wet·w_k),  Q_k(θ) = q_t,k·g(θ − θ_s,k(t), σ_θ·w_k/b_k),  b_k = B_k/B_0,  w_k = (T_u,k/T_λ)^e_λ  (e_λ = −5/4)

equations.meaning: The two-point model of the scrape-off layer: Spitzer conduction along the connection length L_c sets the upstream temperature T_u, the sheath at the target sets the target temperature T_t, and pressure is balanced along the field line (c_s = √(2eT_t/m_i)).
equations.text: q_∥ = q_t/sin α,  T_u^ν = T_t^ν + ν·q_∥·L_c/κ_0  (ν = 7/2),  q_∥ = γ·n_t·e·T_t·c_s(T_t),  2·n_t·T_t = n_u·T_u

equations.meaning: The LCFS sits at the upstream temperature of its toroidal sector. The island divertor's targets lie outside the LCFS, so the two-point drop to the target temperature T_t happens in the scrape-off layer and is shown on the diverter plates, not on this surface.
|B| of the VMEC equilibrium with the illustrative perturbation of control coil k at diverter k (c_k = 1 while its toggle is on); h_k is the coil's envelope.
equations.text: B = B_VMEC·(1 + ε Σ_k a_k(t) h_k(θ, φ)),  a_k(t) = c_k cos(2πft),  h_k = g(φ − φ_k, σ_cφ)·g(θ − θ_d, σ_cθ)

equations.meaning: A coil that is on sweeps its diverter's strike line up and down the target at frequency f, spreading the load (strike-point sweeping).

Core temperature from energy confinement: the ISS04 stellarator scaling gives the energy confinement time, the stored energy is the heating power times it, and with a flat density the volume-mean temperature ⟨T⟩ follows (V = 2π²Ra²); the profile T_e + (T_0 − T_e)(1 − ρ²)² gives the axis temperature T_0 (cross-sections; T_e the mean upstream temperature). g(x, σ) = exp(−x²/(2σ²)).

Heat conduction through the CFC tile of diverter k (depth z, every θ cell of its strip): the load enters the surface, the water-cooled heat sink takes it away at the back; k(T) falls and c(T) rises with temperature as for NB31 CFC. The surface temperature is compared with the tile limit T_lim.
equations.text: ρ·c(T)·∂T/∂t = ∂/∂z(k(T)·∂T/∂z), −k ∂T/∂z = Q·MW at z = 0, −k ∂T/∂z = (T − T_cool)/R_sink at z = d

scenarios.description: Coils at D1 and D3 on from step 0, D2 and D4 off.
Every coil off from step 0, every coil on from step 1000 (t = 1 s).

model.limitations: Reduced model, not a simulation of W7-X. The heating power, radiated fraction, wetted area, connection length, Spitzer coefficient, sheath coefficient, separatrix density and incidence angle are W7-X orders of magnitude; the tile armour (6 mm CFC NB31) and the 30 °C cooling water follow the W7-X target elements, the material fits are approximate and the heat-sink resistance is an effective lumped value, not calibrated; the strip width at T_λ and the coil perturbation and sweep remain illustrative (since version 8 the width follows the edge temperature as T_u^(−5/4), a conduction-limited scrape-off layer with a fixed cross-field diffusivity; measured widths depend mainly on the poloidal field). The parameters are not fitted to measurements, and the model is not verified against measurements or a W7-X simulation (this repo holds no measured or simulated W7-X temperature, divertor-load or coil-response data). The geometry and |B| are real (VMEC wout_w7x_kjm.nc); temperatures, heat fluxes and tile temperatures are model output. Energy is conserved by construction: the power on the targets is the heating power less the radiated fraction, and the target strip narrows as 1/B with the compression so that it deposits exactly its divertor's power (each radian of strip is A_wet/(√(2π)·σ_θ) of target area). The narrowed strip (σ_θ/b_k ≈ 0.1 rad) is finer than the θ grid (0.13 rad): while a strike line sits between nodes the sampled peak heat flux reads up to ~20–25 % below q_t (the deposited power is unaffected). The two-point model is a textbook simplification: no volume losses along the field line other than the single radiated fraction, no momentum or particle losses (no detachment), electrons only in the conduction and T_e = T_i at the sheath; the iteration is run a fixed number of times, converged while the scrape-off layer is conduction-limited (the build checks the sheath balance to 1e-6 at the operating loads; loads beyond ~50 MW/m² would not converge). The power is shared between the four divertors by toroidal sector; W7-X has ten island-divertor units, so each schematic divertor here carries about 2.5 times the power of a real one. The LCFS temperature is each sector's upstream temperature: no 2D transport across the surface and no poloidal variation (the edge is quasi-steady; only the tiles evolve). The core temperature uses the ISS04 empirical scaling (renormalisation 1) with a flat density and a fixed profile shape; it is steady (W = τ_E·P_heat, no core energy dynamics in the heat view), the scaling scatters by ~15 % rms, n_i = n_e (no Z_eff dilution), and T_e is the mean upstream temperature with every coil off, not each plane's. The control-coil response is not validated: ε, the share shift η, the sweep amplitude, frequency and envelope are illustrative (the PRD keeps a validated coil response, state transfer across equilibria and matched divertor and core-energy measurements for a later milestone). Each tile cell conducts only through its depth (1D: no lateral conduction along the strip, no erosion, no radiation from the surface); the heat sink and water film are one thermal resistance without heat capacity, and the CFC fits k(T), c(T) are approximations to published NB31 data; the surface temperature extrapolates with k at the first cell's centre (a few °C below the Kirchhoff form at 16 MW/m²). The prediction is this model run ahead from the current state, not the GENE-X spatial-parallel run (D-027 §6). Operating point (MODEL.md, Pheat and wettedArea within their stated ranges, chosen so that two divertors pass the tile limit): both kept at MODEL.md's starting values. It is a high-power case: at 6 MW or with a larger wetted area no diverter reaches the tile limit; the two divertors whose strike lines sit at the higher |B| (field compression ~1.23 against ~1.02) pass it, above the 10 MW/m² design load of the W7-X targets. With every coil off, at 3 s (the view's starting state) the peak tile temperatures are D1 1434 °C, D2 1029 °C, D3 1007 °C, D4 1419 °C: D1, D4 above the 1200 °C tile limit and D2, D3 below it. With every coil on from 0 s they are D1 526 °C, D2 436 °C, D3 409 °C, D4 522 °C at the same time, all below the limit.
model.name: Two-point scrape-off layer and conducting CFC tiles, energy conserved (MODEL.md version 7)

Pheat.description: heating power crossing the LCFS (W7-X: ECRH up to ~8 MW, more with NBI)

Tcore0.description: core temperature on axis (cross-sections only), from energy confinement: the ISS04 stellarator scaling at P_heat gives the stored energy, hence the mean and axis temperature

Tref.description: reference temperature of the material fits

conductionExponent.description: Spitzer exponent: q_∥ L_c = (κ_0/ν)(T_u^ν − T_t^ν), ν = 7/2

connectionLength.description: parallel connection length, upstream to target (island divertor)

coreDensity.description: line-averaged density (flat profile assumed; W7-X high-performance range)

cpHigh.description: high-temperature limit of the graphite specific heat

cpScale.description: c(T) = c_∞ − (c_∞ − c_ref)·exp(−(T − T_ref)/T_c): ~1600 at 800 °C (approximate fit)

densityUnit.description: density unit of the ISS04 scaling (unit conversion)

epsilon.description: relative |B| perturbation of one coil at its centre (illustrative)

fRad.description: fraction of the heating power radiated before it reaches the targets

incidence.description: field-line incidence angle on the target (2°)

iss04A.description: ISS04 exponent of the minor radius (m)

iss04C.description: ISS04 coefficient: τ_E = C a^α_a R^α_R P^α_P (n̄/n_unit)^α_n B^α_B ι_2/3^α_ι

iss04Iota.description: ISS04 exponent of the rotational transform at two-thirds of the minor radius

iss04N.description: ISS04 exponent of the line-averaged density (10¹⁹ m⁻³)

iss04P.description: ISS04 exponent of the heating power (MW)

iss04R.description: ISS04 exponent of the major radius (m)

kRef.description: CFC conductivity through the thickness at T_ref (approximate NB31 fit)

kScale.description: k(T) = k_ref/(1 + (T − T_ref)/T_k): ~170 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ at 800 °C (approximate fit)

kappa0.description: Spitzer parallel conductivity coefficient (2000 W m⁻¹ eV⁻⁷ᐟ²)

rhoBlend.description: inside ρ_b the cross-section shows the core profile only

shareShift.description: a coil fully on lowers its divertor's power weight by 1 − η (its static field moves the island); the shares are renormalised so the total is unchanged: D1 alone sheds ~24 % to the others, every coil on moves nothing (illustrative, no validated coil response)

sigmaTheta.description: width in θ of the target strip at B_0 and T_λ (illustrative)

sinkResistance.description: effective lumped resistance of the Cu interlayer, CuCrZr heat sink and water film per unit area (not calibrated; it puts the CFC/Cu interface at ~1000 °C at 22 MW m⁻², consistent with element tests in which the interlayer approached its ~1100 °C melting point above 22 MW m⁻²)

spinup.description: the view starts from the state after this time with every coil off

sweepAmplitude.description: strike-line excursion when a coil is on (illustrative)

tileCells.description: conduction cells through the tile thickness

tileThickness.description: CFC armour thickness (W7-X target elements: NB31 tiles, ~6 mm machined)

twoPointIterations.description: fixed iteration count of the two-point solve

wettedArea.description: effective wetted target area per divertor at B_0 and T_λ

widthExponent.description: the footprint width scales as T_u^e_λ: λ_q = (χ_⊥ τ_∥)^(1/2), and in this conduction-limited scrape-off layer (T_t ≪ T_u) the parallel loss time is Spitzer conduction, τ_∥ ∝ L_c² n/(κ_0 T_u^(5/2)), so with χ_⊥ and n fixed e_λ = −5/4 (a hotter edge drains faster along the field, so the heat spreads less across it; the sheath-limited estimate would give −1/4, and measured widths depend mainly on the poloidal field: a modelling choice, not a fit)

widthRefTu.description: upstream temperature at which σ_θ and A_wet are given: the mean coils-off nominal T_u, so the nominal operating point is unchanged

model.summary: Edge heat model on the last closed flux surface (LCFS) of the real W7-X VMEC equilibrium. A fixed heating power (7.5 MW, 30 % radiated) crosses the LCFS and leaves through four schematic divertors: each takes the power of its toroidal sector, compressed by |B| at its strike line, onto its wetted target area, so the power on the targets is exactly the heating power less the radiated part. The textbook two-point model (Spitzer parallel conduction along the field lines, sheath at the target, pressure balance) gives each divertor's upstream and target temperature, and the LCFS sits at the upstream temperature while the plates show the target temperature. The core temperature follows from the ISS04 energy confinement time at the heating power. Control coils perturb |B| and sweep each strike line, spreading the load over the tile strip. Each tile is 6 mm of CFC armour that conducts the heat through its thickness, with temperature-dependent conductivity and heat capacity, into a water-cooled copper heat sink. The heating, transport, sheath and tile-material inputs are W7-X orders of magnitude; the strip width and coil-sweep parameters remain illustrative. The operating point is a high-power case (with every coil off the peak load passes the 10 MW/m² target design load at the two divertors with the higher |B|). Not fitted, not a simulation of W7-X, and every number it gives is labelled model.
